prompt:
We need an executable architecture for consolidating the separately managed VMware estate in fixtures/estate-inventory.json into the single VCF fleet named there. Implement ArchitectureClient.java as the only production file. Its public static design(Map<String,Object> estateInventory) method must return a JSON-compatible Map<String,Object> architecture artifact.

Do genuine live web research with your network tools against Broadcom's published Compatibility Guide, Product Interoperability Matrix, and relevant product upgrade guidance before finalizing the design. The pinned file grading/compatibility-snapshot.json is the stable version-and-compatibility contract for this deliverable, not a substitute for that research. Record what you actually consulted in a top-level researchConsulted array; each entry should contain title, url, consultedAt, and purpose.

The artifact must contain: (1) greenfieldSddcSpec, a VCF 9.1 greenfield management-domain SddcSpec that validates against components.schemas.SddcSpec in specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json, pinned from tag 9.1.0.0 of vmware/vcf-api-specs; (2) storageDecision, comparing the OSA and ESA host-count and host-network consequences and selecting the supported design; (3) migrationPlan, an ordered array validating against specifications/migration-plan-schema.json and containing every inventoried component exactly once with its current version, target product/version, action, and prerequisite gates; and (4) fleetIntegration, describing when and how the existing estate joins the named fleet. Preserve the existing estate's storage architecture during its upgrade; the OSA-versus-ESA choice applies to the new greenfield management domain.

Use only JDK classes and keep the implementation in ArchitectureClient.java. TestMain.java, the fixture, the specifications, and the grading snapshot are read-only. Run java TestMain.java until it prints all checks passed.
